title: NIST AM-Bench 2022 bridge, IN718, built layer by layer and cut from the plate
about: The scenario of the metal printing film (tools/render/README.md, section 'The metal printing film'). The part, the strain, the material and the cut are exactly those of the blind prediction in GOALS.md G20 step 3 (tools/g20_bridge.py predict); only the element size differs, finer at the same 0.5 mm simulation layer, which is the discretisation the strain was calibrated at (lpbf-build.md V6: halving the element size at the same layer thickness is a discretisation change; halving the layer is a change of physics).

part.name: bridge
part.source: NIST AM-Bench 2022, AMB2022-01 part CAD (AMB2022-01-AMMT-PartCAD.STL, a US government work), fetched with the owner's approval on 2026-10-08 for GOALS.md G20 step 3; not held by this repository. Drawn with the pointed end, the base that stays on the plate, at x = 0, so it is built as drawn

material.name: IN718, room-temperature datasheet elastic constants
material.source: Special Metals INCONEL 718 datasheet, 70 F: E = 29.0e6 psi, nu = 0.294 (as tools/g20_bridge.py); the displacement of a body loaded only by an eigenstrain does not depend on E, the stress does

inherent_strain.source: GOALS.md G20 step 3: fitted on NIST AM-Bench AMB2018-01 (IN625 bridge), its free-end ridge measured 1.276 mm, at 0.5 mm layers
inherent_strain.note: one isotropic strain fitted on a published measurement, the free-end ridge of NIST AM-Bench's 2018 IN625 bridge (AMB2018-01, 1.276 mm after the cut), at 0.5 mm layers and elements; at a unit strain of -0.001 that ridge rose 0.3367 mm (GOALS.md G20 step 3)

cut.note: as GOALS.md G20 step 3: NIST cut the twelve legs as close to the plate as possible, no height stated; the bottom 0.5 mm of every leg is removed (two element rows at 0.25 mm), from 20 mm from the pointed end on; the base, the first 19 mm, stays on the plate

supports_note: none: NIST built the bridge without supports, and the overhang rule (45 degrees) finds none, its arches being steeper than that
probes_note: NIST's measured ridges 1 to 6 of the 2022 bridge, every other ridge from the pointed end (centres at X_sq 70.5 to 0.5 mm, here x = 75 - X_sq), each read at the centre of its top, a quarter layer below it, as tools/g20_bridge.py reads them; the deflection is u_z after the cut minus before

record.source: GOALS.md G20 step 3 (2026-10-08), the public record; docs/map/PHYSICS.md and the build summary's scope.measured_accuracy quote it

film.title: Printing NIST's AM-Bench bridge in Inconel 718
film.caption: NIST AM-Bench 2022 bridge, Inconel 718, printed layer by layer and cut from the plate
